name: Shaaph
overview: Shaaph was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Jahdai. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided in Scripture. This places him within the broader context of Judah's lineage as recorded in the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaaph appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin indicated. There is only one recorded name for him, and no special title or meaning is attached to it in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Shaaph is explicitly identified as the son of Jahdai according to the biblical record. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or other relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Shaaph’s significance lies in his role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:47. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion helps preserve the lineage through which God's promises to Judah were fulfilled. His mention underscores the importance of genealogies in tracing God’s covenantal faithfulness throughout Israel’s history.
